taxonomyNote: ADW's account uses the older genus name Bufo (Bufo quercicus); NatureServe uses Anaxyrus quercicus.
fieldMarks: Smallest toad in North America, 1.9-3.3 cm, with a short head, pointed nose and flat body.
Black or brown with a long pale dorsal stripe (white, cream, yellow or orange) and 4-5 pairs of dark blotches; fine reddish bumps give a rough texture.
Elongated teardrop-shaped parotoid glands; grey-white, unblotched underside; males have dusky throats.
Adults can be mistaken for half-grown southern toads.
behavior: More diurnal than most toads, sheltering by day buried in sand or under leaves or rocks; solitary outside breeding, when it may call at night.
Male call is a high-pitched, bird-like chirp.
Eats small terrestrial insects and arthropods such as ants and beetles; most active during the breeding period.
habitat: Sandy pine flatwoods, oak scrub, open pine and pine-oak woods, savannas with sandy soil and maritime forest, favouring open-canopy pine flatwoods with grassy cover; eggs and larvae develop in rain pools, ditches and flatwoods ponds.
range: NatureServe lists it in the southeastern coastal plain: Virginia, North and South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana.
